'''Douglas Richard McDermott''' (born January 3, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). While playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]], McDermott led the nation in scoring in [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14]] and was a three-time consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. He was the consensus [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]] as a senior in 2014, and finished his college career with the fifth-most points in [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] men's basketball history.

After graduating from Creighton, McDermott was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] with the 11th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. He was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] and went on to play two and a half seasons for the Bulls before being traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in February 2017. McDermott has also played for the [[New York Knicks]], the [[Dallas Mavericks]], the [[Indiana Pacers]], and the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. A [[small forward]], McDermott is known for his outside shooting.

McDermott is the son of Creighton coach [[Greg McDermott]] and was coached by his father during his college career.

==High school career==
McDermott was born in [[Grand Forks, North Dakota]], where his father was an assistant coach of the [[North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball|University of North Dakota's men's basketball]] team. McDermott, a 6'7" 225-pound [[Forward (basketball)|forward]], played high school basketball at [[Ames High School]] in [[Ames, Iowa]] alongside high school All-American [[Harrison Barnes]]. Ames won 53 consecutive games during McDermott's and Barnes' junior and senior seasons and won consecutive [[Iowa]] state titles. As a senior, McDermott averaged 20.1 [[points per game|points]] and 7.8 [[rebounds per game]] and was named first team All-State.<ref name=BIO>{{cite web|url=http://www.gocreighton.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1075|title=Doug McDermott Bio|work=GoCreighton.com|access-date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>

Considered a three-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], McDermott was listed as the No. 28 small forward in the nation in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/97963/doug-mcdermott |title=Doug McDermott Recruiting Profile |work=ESPN.com |access-date=February 11, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304100108/http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/97963/doug-mcdermott |archive-date=March 4, 2016 }}</ref>

==College career==
Originally, McDermott signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play with [[Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball|Northern Iowa]], but after his father moved from coaching [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State University]] to [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], he was released from his commitment in order to play for him in college.

As a freshman in [[2010–11 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|2010–11]], McDermott averaged 14.9 points and 7.2 rebounds per game as he started all 39 games for the Bluejays. McDermott set a [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) record for points by a freshman (581) and was named conference freshman and newcomer of the year. McDermott also became the first player to earn first team all-conference honors as a freshman since Cleo Littleton of [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] in 1954.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mvc-sports.com/mbasketball/news/2010-11/5114/weems-is-larry-bird-player-of-the-year/|title=Weems is Larry Bird Player of the Year|publisher=Missouri Valley Conference|date=March 1, 2011|access-date=January 4, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714141039/http://www.mvc-sports.com/mbasketball/news/2010-11/5114/weems-is-larry-bird-player-of-the-year/|archive-date=July 14, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> McDermott led the Bluejays to the [[2011 College Basketball Invitational]], where they made it to the best of three final series, ultimately losing to [[2010–11 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]].<ref name=BIO/>

Prior to his sophomore season, McDermott was named to the preseason watch lists for the [[Wooden Award]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1105 |title=John R. Wooden Award Announces Men's Preseason Top 50 List |publisher=Wooden Award |date=October 3, 2011 |access-date=December 30, 2011 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120403035926/http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1105 |archive-date=April 3, 2012 }}</ref> and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2011/11/2011-12-naismith-trophy-preseason-watch-list/|title=2011–12 Naismith Trophy Preseason Watch List|publisher=Slam Magazine|date=November 8, 2011|access-date=December 30, 2011}}</ref>

As a sophomore, McDermott was one of five men named first team All-America for the 2011–12 season. McDermott is Creighton's first player honored by the NABC on its first-team All-America squad. McDermott also was named the [[Missouri Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Missouri Valley Conference Player of the Year]], the first Creighton player since [[Booker Woodfox]] in 2009. McDermott finished his 2011–12 season averaging 22.9 points per game, a figure that ranked third nationally. His 801 points, 307 field goals, and 48.6 percent shooting accuracy from three-point range were all school records for a single season.  Creighton finished 29–6 and advanced to the Third Round (now Second Round) of the NCAA tournament. On March 26, 2012, McDermott was named a first-team AP [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mvcstcharles.com/news/archives/2011-12/5917/nabc-names-mcdermott-first-team-all-american/ |title=NABC Names McDermott First-Team All-American |work=mvcstcharles.com |date=March 21, 2012 |access-date=February 11, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160216104608/http://www.mvcstcharles.com/news/archives/2011-12/5917/nabc-names-mcdermott-first-team-all-american/ |archive-date=February 16, 2016 }}</ref>

As a junior in [[2012–13 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|2012–13]], McDermott ranked first in the nation in points scored and second in points per game. He set school records for points in a single season and in a career. He was again named a first-team All-American by the AP.<ref name=BIO/>

On April 25, 2013, McDermott announced he would be returning to Creighton for his senior season and would not enter the [[2013 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Gleeson|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/04/25/creightons-doug-mcdermott-announces-his-return-skips-nba/2113313/|title=Creighton's Doug McDermott announces his return|work=USAToday.com|date=April 25, 2013|access-date=April 25, 2013}}</ref> That July, he relinquished his scholarship and became a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] for his final season at Creighton. This came about after the NCAA had granted senior guard [[Grant Gibbs (basketball)|Grant Gibbs]], who had missed full seasons at both [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and Creighton with injuries, a rare sixth year of eligibility, putting Creighton over the NCAA's limit of 13 scholarships for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9444744/grant-gibbs-creighton-bluejays-gets-sixth-year-eligibility|title=Grant Gibbs granted sixth year|work=ESPN.com|date=July 2, 2013|access-date=August 19, 2013}}</ref>

McDermott led the nation in scoring at 26.7 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/stats/player?season=2014|title=2013-14 NCAA Division I College Basketball Player Statistics|work=ESPN.com|access-date=March 31, 2014}}</ref> At the end of his college career, he ranked fifth on the all-time NCAA Division I scoring list, with 3,150 points, which passed basketball Hall of Famer [[Larry Bird]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/doug-mcdermott-1.html|title=Doug McDermott College Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 23, 2014}}</ref> He became the first player in 29 years to be named to the AP All-America first team three times.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10702957/doug-mcdermott-unanimous-choice-ap-all-america-team|title=Doug McDermott makes 3rd AP team|work=ESPN.com|date=March 31, 2014|access-date=March 31, 2014}}</ref> McDermott is one of three players in NCAA men's basketball history to record 3,000 points and 1,000 rebounds. He also set an NCAA record by scoring in double figures in 135 games.<ref name=BIO/>

==Professional career==
===Chicago Bulls (2014–2017)===
====2014–15 season====
On June 26, 2014, McDermott was selected in the first round with the 11th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He was later traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] on draft night, along with [[Anthony Randolph]], for both of Chicago's 2014 first-round picks ([[Jusuf Nurkic]] 16th and [[Gary Harris]] 19th) and a future second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/06/26/nuggets-take-mcdermitt-062614.ap/|title=Bulls deal picks for Doug McDermott|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=June 26, 2014}}</ref> On July 22, 2014, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Bulls after averaging 18.0 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game during the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-forward-doug-mcdermott|title=BULLS SIGN FORWARD DOUG MCDERMOTT|work=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2014|access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref> In his NBA debut on October 29, he recorded 12 points, 5 rebounds, 2 assists and 1 steal in a 104–80 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Mahoney|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/CHINYK/gameinfo.html|title=Gasol, Bulls blow out Knicks in Rose's return|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=October 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150430045255/http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/CHINYK/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 30, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

While expected to contribute with scoring and shooting for the Bulls, McDermott struggled significantly over his first 17 games, averaging just 3.2 points on 42.3 percent shooting.<ref>{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Freeman|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/doug-mcdermott-to-undergo-knee-surgery--continuing-a-rough-season-022147273.html|title=Doug McDermott to undergo knee surgery, continuing a rough season|work=Yahoo.com|date=December 12, 2014|access-date=December 12, 2014}}</ref> Despite his promising debut, McDermott did not manage to eclipse 12 points before being ruled out indefinitely on December 1 due to a knee injury. He subsequently required an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee which took place on December 13.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/doug-mcdermott-injury-update|title=DOUG MCDERMOTT INJURY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=December 12, 2014|access-date=December 12, 2014}}</ref> He returned to action on January 22, 2015, against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], recording no stats in two minutes of action.<ref>{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Seligman|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150122/SASCHI/gameinfo.html|title=Derrick Rose scores 22, struggling Bulls beat Spurs 104-81|work=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2015|access-date=January 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150123013828/http://www.nba.com/games/20150122/SASCHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 23, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 6, he scored a season-high 16 points in a loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Marot|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150306/CHIIND/gameinfo.html|title=Pacers hold off charging Bulls 98-84 for 4th straight win|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2015|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mcderdo01/gamelog/2015/|title=Doug McDermott 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref>

====2015–16 season====
In July 2015, McDermott re-joined the Bulls for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 18.8 points and 4.4 rebounds in five games, impressing new head coach [[Fred Hoiberg]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Steven|last=Pivovar|url=http://www.omaha.com/creighton/doug-mcdermott-scores-well-impresses-new-bulls-coach-in-summer/article_f692f6b0-5b63-58db-8e0d-e59ea0443d84.html|title=Doug McDermott scores well, impresses new Bulls coach in Summer League|work=Omaha.com|date=July 25, 2015|access-date=July 25, 2015}}</ref> On October 30, the Bulls exercised their third-year team option on McDermott's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/bulls-exercise-options-snell-and-mcdermott/|title=BULLS EXERCISE OPTIONS ON SNELL AND MCDERMOTT|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2015|access-date=October 30, 2015}}</ref>

====2016–17 season====
On October 28, 2016, the Bulls exercised their fourth-year team option on McDermott's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-exercise-options-mcdermott-grant-and-portis/|title=BULLS EXERCISE OPTIONS ON MCDERMOTT, GRANT AND PORTIS|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}}</ref> Among other moves that offseason, the Bulls also acquired Chicago native [[Dwyane Wade]], for whom McDermott switched from No. 3 to No. 11 for the 2016–17 season. In the Bulls' second game of the season, McDermott scored a game-high 23 points off the bench in a 118–101 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899480|title=Butler, Wade, Rondo lead Bulls to 118-101 rout of Pacers|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}}</ref> He received a concussion on October 31 against the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and entered concussion protocol; on November 12, he suffered another concussion against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Brown|first=Larry|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/bulls-mcdermott-in-concussion-protocol/ar-AAkfyBI/|title=Doug McDermott enteres concussion protocol after Halloween|work=MSN.com|date=November 13, 2016|access-date=November 13, 2016}}</ref> As a result, McDermott missed the next nine games, and on December 5, he was assigned to the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA Development League]] for conditioning.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://windycity.dleague.nba.com/news/chicago-bulls-assign-doug-mcdermott-windy-city/|title=Chicago Bulls Assign Doug McDermott to Windy City|work=NBA.com|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref> He was recalled two days later<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/bulls-recall-mcdermott-from-d-league-s-windy-city-bulls-120716|title=Bulls recall McDermott from D-League's Windy City Bulls|work=FoxSports.com|date=December 7, 2016|access-date=December 7, 2016}}</ref> and made his return to Chicago's line-up on December 8, scoring eight points in a 95–91 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899778|title=Spurs fall to Bulls 95-91 after winning first 13 road games|work=ESPN.com|date=December 8, 2016|access-date=December 9, 2016}}</ref>

On January 7, 2017, McDermott recorded his first-career double-double, grabbing a career-high 10 rebounds to go with 17 points in a 123–118 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=K.C.|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-bulls-closing-lineup-bits-spt-0109-20170108-story.html|title=Fred Hoiberg gives new look to Bulls' closing lineup|work=ChicagoTribune.com|date=January 8, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}}</ref> On January 15, 2017, he scored a career-high 31 points in a 108–104 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900032|title=McDermott scores career-best 61 to lead Bulls past Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=January 15, 2017}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2017)===
On February 23, 2017, McDermott was traded, along with [[Taj Gibson]] and an [[Mitchell Robinson|unprotected 2018 second round draft pick]], to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Joffrey Lauvergne]], [[Anthony Morrow]] and [[Cameron Payne]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/gibson-mcdermott-170223|title=Thunder Acquires Gibson, McDermott and Draft Pick|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}}</ref> On March 18, 2017, McDermott had his highest-scoring game with the Thunder, going 8 of 9 from the field, including 4 of 5 from three-point range, to finish with 21 points in a 110–94 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400900423|title=Westbrook leads Thunder past Kings without triple-double|work=ESPN.com|date=March 18, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2017–2018)===
On September 25, 2017, McDermott was traded, along with [[Enes Kanter]] and a [[Mitchell Robinson|2018 second-round pick]], to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Carmelo Anthony]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/features/knicks-trade-carmelo-anthony-oklahoma-city|title=Knicks Trade Carmelo Anthony To Oklahoma City|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2017|access-date=September 25, 2017}}</ref> In his debut for the Knicks in their season opener on October 19, 2017, McDermott scored four points on 2-for-5 shooting in a 105–84 loss to his former team, the [[2017–18 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974441|title=Thunder top Knicks 105-84 in OKC debuts for George, Anthony|work=ESPN.com|date=October 19, 2017|access-date=October 20, 2017}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2018)===
On February 8, 2018, McDermott was acquired by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in a three-team trade that also involved the Knicks and the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-acquire-doug-mcdermott-second-round-pick-three-team-trade/|title=Mavs acquire Doug McDermott and second-round pick in three-team trade|work=Mavs.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018|archive-date=February 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180209223434/https://www.mavs.com/mavs-acquire-doug-mcdermott-second-round-pick-three-team-trade/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his debut for the Mavericks two days later, McDermott scored eight points in a 130–123 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 10, 2018 |title=Nowitzki, Mavs spoil Thomas debut in 130-123 win over Lakers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975576 |access-date=February 11, 2018 |work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He received a qualifying offer from the Mavericks on June 27, 2018, but the offer was later withdrawn.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/26/reports-yogi-ferrell-salah-mejri-qualifying-offer-mcdermott-withdrawn|title=Reports: Yogi Ferrell, Salah Mejri get qualifying offers; Doug McDermott's qualifying offer withdrawn|work=nba.com|date=June 27, 2018|access-date=June 27, 2018}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2018–2021)===
On July 6, 2018, McDermott signed a three-year, $22 million contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-tyreke-evans-doug-mcdermott|title=Pacers Sign Tyreke Evans, Doug McDermott|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23959094/doug-mcdermott-indiana-pacers-agree-3-year-22m-deal|title=Sources: Doug McDermott, Pacers agree to 3-year, $22M deal|work=[[ESPN]]|date=July 1, 2018|access-date=July 1, 2018}}</ref> On November 26, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 121–88 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 26, 2018 |title=McDermott, Turner lead Pacers to 121-88 rout of Jazz |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070980 |access-date=November 27, 2018 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On May 1, 2021, McDermott scored a career-high-tying 31 points, making a season-high six 3-pointers in a 152–95 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Stinar|first=Ben|title=Pacers' Doug McDermott Scored a Career-High Against the Thunder|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/news/pacers-doug-mcdermott-scored-a-career-high-against-the-thunder|url-status=live|access-date=2021-05-03|website=Sports Illustrated|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503013448/https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/news/pacers-doug-mcdermott-scored-a-career-high-against-the-thunder |archive-date=May 3, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Pacers' Doug McDermott: Drains six threes in laugher|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-doug-mcdermott-drains-six-threes-in-laugher/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-05-03|website=CBSSports.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503013449/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-doug-mcdermott-drains-six-threes-in-laugher/ |archive-date=May 3, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Game Rewind: Pacers 152, Thunder 95|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/rewind-pacers-thunder-210501|url-status=live|access-date=2021-05-03|website=Indiana Pacers|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502024950/https://www.nba.com/pacers/rewind-pacers-thunder-210501 |archive-date=May 2, 2021 }}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2021–2024)===
On August 8, 2021, McDermott joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] via a [[sign-and-trade deal]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire Doug Mcdermott|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-acquire-doug-mcdermott|website=NBA.com|date=August 8, 2021|access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> in which McDermott agreed to a three-year, $42 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Zucker|title=Spurs Rumors: Doug McDermott Agrees to 3-Year, $42M Contract at Start of Free Agency|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10009481-spurs-rumors-doug-mcdermott-agrees-to-3-year-42m-contract-at-start-of-free-agency|website=BleacherReport.com|date=August 2, 2021|access-date=August 2, 2021}}</ref> On March 12, 2022, he suffered a right ankle injury in a 108–119 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. Four days later, it was announced that the injury was diagnosed as a grade 3 ankle sprain, sidelining McDermott for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Petrini|title=Doug McDermott expected to miss remainder of season with ankle sprain, Spurs announce|url=https://www.kens5.com/article/sports/nba/spurs/doug-mcdermott-expected-to-miss-remainder-of-season-with-ankle-sprain-spurs-announce/273-88f878d1-dd17-409d-8a60-9d4ae9a27754|work=[[KENS|KENS 5]]|date=March 16, 2022|access-date=March 16, 2022}}</ref>

===Second stint with Pacers (2024)===
On February 8, 2024, McDermott was traded back to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in a three-team deal, sending [[Buddy Hield]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Complete Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-complete-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2024–2026)===
On October 16, 2024, McDermott signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Announce Roster Changes|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-roster-changes|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref>

On July 21, 2025, McDermott re-signed with the Kings on a one-year, $3.6 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Doug McDermott to return to Kings on one-year, $3.6M deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45788986/doug-mcdermott-return-kings-one-year-36m-deal|access-date=July 27, 2025|website=espn.com|language=es}}</ref>

==National team career==
Following the close of his freshman year at Creighton, McDermott was selected to the U.S. team sent to [[Riga]], [[Latvia]] for the 2011 [[FIBA Under-19 World Championship]].  McDermott started all nine matches and averaged 11.3 points per game on .501 shooting and 6.1 rebounds per contest, good for third on the team in both categories. The United States finished 7–2, good for fifth in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/u19/mu19_2011.html |title=Tenth FIBA U19 World Championship 2011 |work=USABasketball.com |publisher=USA Basketball |year=2011 |access-date=January 4, 2012 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130602214216/http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/u19/mu19_2011.html |archive-date=June 2, 2013 }}</ref>

On July 22, 2014, McDermott was named to the 2014 USA Select Team.<ref>{{cite web|title=BUTLER AND MCDERMOTT NAMED TO 2014 USA SELECT TEAM|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/butler-and-mcdermott-named-2014-usa-select-team|work=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2014|access-date=July 23, 2014}}</ref>
